The *Fahua Lingyan Zhuan* (Biographies of Miraculous Responses to the Lotus Sutra), Volume One.
Regarding the *Fahua Lingyan Zhuan*, there is the ten-volume *Hongzan Zhuan* (Extolled Biographies) compiled by the Śramaṇa Huiding of Langu in the Great Tang;
the four-volume *Xianying Lu* (Record of Manifested Responses) compiled by the Śramaṇa Zongxiao of Siming in the Great Song; and furthermore—
There exists a four-fascicle work titled *Hae-dong jeon-hong nok* (Records of the Propagation in the Land of the Eastern Sea), compiled by National Preceptor Jinging of our own dynasty.
Having now perused these three biographies in their entirety, I have excerpted the most extraordinary events from among them and combined them into two fascicles to inspire future generations.
These two fascicles comprise one hundred and seven marvelous and unique accounts.
Contemplating Consciousness: A Discourse by the Śramaṇa Shi Liaoyuan, Presented as a Record of the Garden of Millet Seeding Auspiciousness (*yǐ* is pronounced *yǐ*; it is a fragrant herb).
The Dharma Master Kumārajīva—here translated as "Child Longevity"—was a native of Kucha (the character *guī* is pronounced *qiū*). He entered the monastic order at the age of seven. Daily...

He recited a thousand verses. His mother took him to the country of Yuezhi, where he met an arhat who said, "This śrāmaṇera, when he reaches the age of thirty-five, shall greatly propagate the Buddha-dharma and deliver countless people. His mother always held these words in high regard. One day, the arhat said to her:

"The profound teachings of the Vaipulya sutras ought to be widely propagated in the Land of the Great Red [China]; this depends solely upon your power. At that time, Fu Jian held the region of Guanzhong.

The Grand Astrologer submitted a report stating: "A star of virtue has appeared in the celestial division corresponding to foreign lands; there shall surely be a man of great wisdom who enters to assist the Middle Kingdom."
Fu Jian said, "I have heard that there is a Kumārajīva in the Western Regions; could this not be him? He immediately dispatched Lü Guang to lead troops to invade the kingdom of Kucha.

Once Lü Guang had captured Kumārajīva, he returned to Liangzhou. Upon hearing that Fu Jian had been killed by Yao Chang, he took control of the region beyond the passes and usurped the title of the Later Liang dynasty.
When Yao Chang passed away and his son Yao Xing succeeded to the throne, twin-stemmed trees suddenly grew in the imperial ancestral temple.

In the Xiaoyao Garden, scallions transformed into *yǐ* (wild millet), which was regarded as an auspicious omen. Consequently, he launched a military campaign against Lü Guang and welcomed Kumārajīva to Chang’an, where he honored him with the rites due to a National Teacher.
Yao Xing summoned various śramaṇas to the Xiaoyao Garden to listen to Kumārajīva’s expositions.
Kumārajīva was eloquent and proficient in both Chinese and the languages of the Western Regions.

Observing that the old translations diverged from the Indic original, in the eighth year of the Hongshi era, at Cudeng Temple, he assembled over eight hundred people, including Senglüe (pronounced Lì), as well as more than two thousand śramaṇas from all quarters who were experts in the study of doctrine.
Together they collated the new version against the old translations and translated this *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* in one volume consisting of seven fascicles. — Kumārajīva.

He said, "The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* and other sutras I have translated have fortunately been widely circulated. If my translations are free from error, I pray that after my body is cremated, my tongue will not be scorched or decayed.
Having spoken these words, he passed away. When his cremation took place, the boundary of his tongue was not reduced to ash.

This is clearly recorded in the *Biographies of the Liang Monks* (*Liang seng zhuan*) and the *Record of Miraculous Responses from Mount Nanshan* (*Nanshan gantong zhuan*). The celestial being Wei said, "Master Kumārajīva was brilliant and well-versed in the Mahāyāna. He—

Translated and transmitted since the time of the seven Buddhas, this is the legacy entrusted by the Dharma King. As for the common saying that it violates the precepts, there is no need to doubt this;

Kumārajīva stood among the Three Sages and was no ordinary person. Excerpted from the second volume of the *Hongzan* (Extensive Praise) and the first part of the *Xianying Lu* (Record of Manifest Responses).
When Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty was still a prince in hiding, celestial flowers appeared as an auspicious omen, and his residence emitted light for seven days and seven nights.

The Emperor said, "This is not a dwelling fit for me," and he relinquished it to become a monastery named Guangzhai (Light-Residence). By imperial decree, Dharma Master Fayun was appointed as its abbot. Master Yun was from Yixing Yang...
He was envied by others. At birth, clouds filled his room; he was thus named accordingly. At the age of seven, he left the household life and changed his name to Fayun.

During his years as a *śrāmaṇera*, he held the scriptures and arts in high esteem. He studied the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* with meticulous refinement and repeated reflection, weighing its meanings and principles until he had a clear and comprehensive understanding from beginning to end.
He became renowned during the Liang dynasty. Once, while concluding a lecture on this sūtra at a monastery, he suddenly—

He perceived celestial flowers, resembling flying snow, filling the sky as they descended. They extended into the hall and rose into the air without falling, departing only after the lecture was concluded.
There was a monk who had been his constant attendant and disciple, named Master Faxun, who day and night made vows, hoping to attain wisdom and understanding.
Suddenly, he dreamed of a monk who said, "Master Yun has already expounded this sutra since the time of Dīpaṃkara Buddha; how could you possibly defeat him?
Furthermore, a fisherman in Yiling County found a scroll of the sutra within his net; it was the "Chapter on the Four Dharmas" from the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra*, with the colophon at the end stating:
"In the second year of the Yuanhui era of the Song dynasty, Wang Baosheng made this offering for Master Fayun of Guangzhai Temple. Based on this...
Examine this: in the second year of the Yuanhui era, Master Yun was only ten years old; yet the temple Guangzhai did not yet exist. This was a premonitory manifestation of a spiritual omen.
As soon as the character "Miao" (Wondrous) was first completed, he was born in this supreme place.
During the Kaihuang era of the Sui dynasty, there was a monk named Huichao whose practice was exceptionally eminent. He constantly recited the Lotus Sūtra.
He had a disciple who, having reached the age for study, died suddenly. Not far from Mount Tai, Huichao went there, burned incense, and fully explained his purpose for coming.

The wooden puppet suddenly spoke, saying, "Your Reverence’s precepts and ascetic practices are so refined and rigorous; how could I dare not report what you have asked? He then led [Chao] before the Marquis.
Chao addressed him, saying, "Where am I now, Disciple? The Marquis replied, "You are here; you have not yet reached the place of birth.
Chao said, "May I have an audience with you? The Marquis then had him lead the way eastward for several dozen paces, where they indeed found it.
They met, and [the Master] asked how their suffering and joy were. The disciple said, "I am merely bound and fettered;
I have neither suffering nor joy. I think that my place of rebirth is not yet fixed; I pray that the Master will deliver me. The Master asked, "What merit have you performed?

The disciple requested to commission a copy of the *Lotus Sūtra* and to provide a vegetarian feast for one hundred people. Once the Master had returned, he immediately transcribed the scripture and fed the monks. When these matters were completed, he returned once more.

He went to visit the Prefect, who received him as he had before. The Master related what he had done. The Prefect said, "My disciple’s master has finished copying the title for a scripture with exquisite characters, and [the child] was immediately reborn in a superior place.
The Master asked, "Where was he reborn? The Prefect replied, "He was reborn in the household of Wang Wu of Qijun as a male child.
You may go to seek him out once he is three years old; if more than three years pass, you should go and ask about him. After three years had elapsed, he went there and inquired.
The donor’s son wished to meet him, but the Wang family refused him, claiming they had no son. The Master recounted the words of the Prefect in detail.
His wife, while still in her room, said to her husband, "The Dharma Master’s spiritual efficacy is such as this; you may allow him to see him."
He immediately took his son and placed him outside the boundary; as soon as the boy saw the Master, he ran into his arms and wept bitterly for a long time.

When the boy grew up, he aspired to leave the household life and returned to serve Master Chao. (From the *Lingrui ji*, also appearing in the tenth fascicle of the *Hongzan chuan* and the *Xianying lu*).
The title has just been written when he was released from the Office of the Netherworld.

Sui Dynasty Monk Xingjian constantly practiced meditative contemplation and maintained extremely strict moral integrity. On one occasion, while traveling through Taishan for business, he entered a temple on the mountain at sunset to spend the night.
He spread out some mugwort grass on the veranda and sat upright to recite the sutras. After about one watch of the night, he suddenly saw—
The spirit’s attire was most magnificent, and he joined his palms toward Huijian. Huijian asked, "Is it true, as the world says, that Mount Tai governs the ghosts?
The spirit replied, "I am one of those who possess such knowledge. Huijian said, "There were two fellow monks who have already died; are they here now?
The spirit asked for their names and said, "One has already been reborn among humans, while the other is in hell undergoing retribution. You, Master, may go and see him."

The deity sent a messenger to lead him into the courtyard wall. There he saw a man within the flames, crying out; his form had been transformed beyond recognition, and the stench of scorched flesh and blood was unbearable.
Daojian could not bear to look and immediately returned to the eaves below to sit again with the deity.

Daojian asked, "Is it possible to save this monk? The deity replied, "It can be done. If you can transcribe the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* for him, he will surely be able to escape. Daojian then departed.

He urgently informed [the deity] of his previous vow. Once the copying and binding of the sutra were complete, he carried it to the temple. The deity emerged as before. He informed the deity of what had transpired, and the deity said:
"Because you, Master, wrote the title of the sutra, he has already been reborn among humans. However, this place is impure; it is not appropriate to enshrine the sutra here.
I pray that you return it to a human temple for veneration. —From the *Biographies of Eminent Monks of the Great Song* (Dà Sòng Gāosēng Zhuàn).

**Section One: Preface** At the moment the title was chanted, the hells were all emptied; at the time the paper was purchased, the heavens had already been transformed.
When King Bu-fa chanted the title bestowed by the Emperor of Heaven, the hells were all emptied.
Li Shanlong, a native of Fengyi, was a Left Gate Guard during the Wude era of the Tang dynasty; he died suddenly after seven days had passed.
The man then revived and recounted his experience: "At first, I was pursued by an official to the presence of King Yama.
There I saw thousands of prisoners. The King asked Long, 'What meritorious deeds have you performed? I replied, 'I can recite two fascicles of the Lotus Sūtra. The King exclaimed, 'Excellent!
He immediately ordered a seat to be spread and requested that I recite it. I began chanting the 'Introduction, Chapter One' of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*. The King—"
The King said, "Stop! The dragon then descended from his seat. Looking back at the prisoners, he saw that they had all departed through the air.
The King praised the power of reciting the sutras, saying it enabled all who heard it to attain liberation. The King immediately ordered the dragon to be reborn.

He further commanded a messenger to lead him on a tour of the various hells, so that he might witness the iron cities, boiling cauldrons, and other such horrors. The messenger said, "That you have now been able to escape is entirely due to the [power of the] sutras..."
"By the power of my merit, you shall return and provide me with food. The dragon immediately granted this. Once he had revived, he saw his relatives preparing funeral equipment.
He then dispatched them to prepare food by the water's edge. Suddenly, he saw three men who apologized, saying, "You have not proven unfaithful to your word.
Having spoken, they vanished. (From the *Taiping guangji*).
At the time he purchased the paper, Heaven had already transformed into Luozhou.
A man from Luoyang named He Xuanling died in the capital during the Longshuo era (662–663 CE) and was appointed as a Chief Scribe by the authorities of the underworld.
During the Linde era (664–665 CE), a fellow villager of Ling died and traveled the path to the netherworld, where he encountered Ling. Ling questioned his fellow villager.
"Why have you come this far? He replied, "I was pursued here. Ling said, "I saw that the head of the bureau was lingering;

you have come in vain. Let you go back. As the villager took his leave and was about to depart, he saw a woman from his own village who said to him, "When you arrived here, did you not observe the place where I suffer?
Behold, the cauldrons of boiling oil are surging and cooking [the damned]."
The sinner said, "Mistress, you may tell my husband to have a copy of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* made for me.

If he grants this, you may report to me ten days hence at the water-head to the south of the village. Once the villager had recovered, he immediately summoned his husband and ordered him to transcribe the scripture.
The husband hurriedly purchased paper and entrusted it to a scribe to write it out. When the villager arrived...
On the day before [the appointed time], she went to the riverside. There she encountered another woman, to whom she said, "Are you the person to whom I previously entrusted the copying of the sutra?
The local woman replied, "I am. The woman said, "The husband of the woman from before passed away to the heavens on the very day he purchased the paper.
That is why I was unable to meet with you as scheduled; therefore, I have left [this message]."
He said, "I entrust this message for you to report to my lord. Having finished speaking, he could no longer be seen. This appears in the tenth fascicle of the *Hongzan* (Extensive Praise).
Regarding the King Who Spread His Hair, the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra* states: "In the past, there was an aranyaka bhikṣu in the kingdom of India named Mahāra."
The king of that country once spread his hair over the mud so that the bhikṣus might walk across it.
On another occasion, a bhikṣu came and said to the king, "This man has not read many scriptures; why do you provide him such great offerings?
The king replied, "One day at midnight, I wished to see this bhikṣu, so I went to his place. There I saw this bhikṣu in a cave reciting the Lotus Sūtra."
There was a person of golden radiance riding a white elephant. The King joined his palms in worship. Just as I drew near him, he immediately vanished.
I asked the Great Virtuous One, "Because of my arrival, why has the person of golden radiance disappeared?
The bhikṣu said, "This is the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra. Samantabhadra himself has declared: 'If there is anyone who recites the Lotus Sūtra, I [will appear to them].'"
"He shall come riding upon a white elephant to instruct me. When I recite this sutra, Samantabhadra will come in person.
Samantabhadra is the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra from the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra*. Having heard this, I prostrated at his feet and withdrew.
Therefore, I now constantly make offerings [to him]. [Quoted from] *Hongzan* (Extolling the Propagation), fascicle 9, and *Xianyingshu* (Record of Manifested Responses), fascicle 1.

The Celestial Emperor bestowed gold upon the pure-faith layman Yinming Guan. He was a native of Xiaozou Village in Danyang. In his youth, he had once left the household life, though he possessed no other specialized practice;
he merely recited one copy of the *Lotus Sūtra*. Later, he returned to secular life and took a wife, devoting himself to farming as his livelihood.
Whether she was employed as a palace servant or engaged in manual labor at home, her livelihood was extremely poor and she lacked sufficient food and clothing.
She constantly recited the sutras without ceasing for even a moment; except for sleeping, eating, and attending to official or private affairs, she never let a single day pass in vain.
Later, suddenly in the middle of the night, she heard a voice in the air calling out, "Yinmingguan! Yinmingguan! (O Yinmingguan!)
He called out very clearly. Guanqi responded with an assent. The person in the air spoke again: "Rise up! I shall give you gold and jewels.
The treasure is beneath a large yellow lotus tree at the eastern edge of the fields south of the village. You may go and fetch it. Guanqi felt great joy and immediately rose;
he called his son to bring fire, a spade, and a pickaxe, and they went together to the fields. Seeing his father about to depart, the son still harbored [doubts].
The son said with suspicion and resentment, "How could you suddenly take gold in the middle of the night? My father has gone mad. The father insisted on proceeding and went away.
When he arrived at the foot of the tree and dug there, he saw no gold at all. The son again admonished his father. After a short while, a voice was heard from the air saying, "You may come closer.
Following these words, they took it up and indeed obtained something. Because of this, they established their livelihood and expanded their business.
There was no longer any distress from poverty. The villagers found his conduct so extraordinary that they suspected there must be some other reason.
Dao-guan then explained the matter in detail to the elders, whereupon he applied himself even more diligently to his recitation and study. (Recorded in *Chuhongzan*, fascicle 8.)
